metadata.title: Joel
metadata.subtitle: Joel 1:1 – 3:21 (18 questions)
metadata.description: Questions on the Book of Joel according to the King James Version (1769).
metadata.author: King James Version (1769)

questions.text: What devastation does Joel 1:4 portray as a figure of the coming judgment?

options.text: A grievous drought that dried up the rivers and burned the pleasant pastures
A plague of insects: what the palmerworm left the locust ate, the rest the cankerworm and caterpiller
A mighty earthquake that cast down all the fortified walls of the cities
A deadly pestilence that smote man and beast and left the land desolate

questions.text: What are the priests and elders called upon to do in Joel 1:13-14?

options.text: To muster the men of war and strengthen the high battlements of Zion
To offer new sacrifices in the sanctuary and purify the defiled altars
To lie in sackcloth, sanctify a fast, and cry aloud unto the LORD
To gather all the royal corn into the storehouses and shut the gates

questions.text: How did the beasts groan according to Joel 1:18?

options.text: The cattle fled into the mountains because the fruitful land was spoiled
The herds were torn by wild beasts because the shepherds were gone away
The beasts were brought for sacrifice that the fierce anger might turn
The beasts groan, the herds of cattle are perplexed, having no pasture

questions.text: With what alarm does Joel 2 begin?

options.text: Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, for the day of the LORD cometh
Sound the silver horn in the streets, for a foreign king draweth near
Cry aloud in the gates of the temple, for the holy sacrifice hath ceased
Rend your garments in the court, for the drought hath dried up all wine

questions.text: What true repentance does the LORD require according to Joel 2:13?

options.text: Rend your garments and offer burnt offerings in abundance unto the LORD
Rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God
Fast seven days and keep silence before the LORD in sackcloth and ashes
Bring the tithes into the house of the LORD and offer there abundantly

questions.text: What does the LORD promise in Joel 2:25?

options.text: To give a plenteous harvest in the next year
To rid the land of the locusts and sow it anew
To restore the years that the locust hath eaten
To give new fields in the valley of Jehoshaphat and bless them

questions.text: What prophecy did Peter quote on the day of Pentecost from Joel 2:28?

options.text: I will bring you again into your land and make you one people again
I will make a new covenant with Israel and build up his house anew
I will send my messenger before thee, which shall prepare thy way before thee
I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy

questions.text: Where will the LORD gather all nations to judge them (Joel 3:2)?

options.text: Into the valley of Jehoshaphat
Upon the holy mount of Carmel
In the fertile plain of Jezreel
In the deep valley of Hinnom

questions.text: What summons is proclaimed unto the Gentiles in Joel 3:10?

options.text: Beat your swords into plowshares, and your spears into pruninghooks
Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruninghooks into spears
Build walls about your cities and arm your men of war
Lay down your weapons and proclaim peace

questions.text: Whose son was the prophet Joel according to Joel 1:1?

options.text: The son of Pethuel
The son of Amoz
The son of Hilkiah
The son of Beeri

questions.text: Order the four destroyers in the sequence they eat according to Joel 1:4.

options.text: Cankerworm
Palmerworm
Caterpiller
Locust

questions.text: How was the land commanded to lament in Joel 1:8?

options.text: Like a widow that casteth ashes upon her head for her son
Like a mother that burieth her child and holdeth her peace
Like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth
Like a shepherd that hath lost all his flock and weepeth

questions.text: How does Joel 2:3 describe the land before and behind the host?

options.text: Before them as a field, behind them as a quarry
Before them as a vineyard, behind them as a marsh
Before them as a wilderness, behind them as the garden of Eden
Before them as the garden of Eden, behind them a desolate wilderness

questions.text: Which two attributes of God does Joel 2:13 declare as reason for turning?

options.text: He is slow to anger, and of great kindness
He is hidden and will not be entreated of men
He is gracious and merciful
He is unyielding and avengeth every sin instantly

questions.text: What prayer should the priests speak between the porch and the altar (Joel 2:17)?

options.text: Spare thy people, O LORD, that the heathen should not rule over them
That the LORD would chasten his people sore, that they might come to themselves
That the LORD would destroy the heathen and utterly lay waste their cities
That the LORD would raise up a new king over his people Israel

questions.text: What does the LORD send down for His people as of old in Joel 2:23?

options.text: Tempest and heavy hail in the winter season
The former rain and the latter rain
Sweet dew and morning mists upon mountains
Manna and quails in abundance every morning

questions.text: With what images does Joel 3:13 call to the judgment of the heathen?

options.text: Kindle the torches, for night is fallen; the towers are overthrown
Yoke the oxen to the plow, for seedtime is come; cisterns are full
Put ye in the sickle, harvest is ripe: press full, fats overflow
Blow the trumpet, for crops are spoiled; all the storehouses empty

questions.text: What blessed fruitfulness shall come upon the mountains in Joel 3:18?

options.text: The mountains shall drop down milk, and hills flow with choice wine
The mountains shall drop down honey, and hills flow with sweet oil
The mountains shall drop down gentle dew, and hills flow with waters
The mountains shall drop down new wine, and hills flow with milk
